# #4593: Patch: the Infinite Assault, C9, Singularity
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

Part of #4601, the cards' fullsend tree (and of the tracker #4576). Card part **C9**: replace the stub scripts
CF (#4602) wrote for the cards below with their scripts and tests, base and Radiant, as cards of a held
single-player set. It builds beside the other card parts on the tree's integration branch; players see nothing
until the release (R).

The plan of record is [`docs/infinite-assault.md`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/claude/gallant-ritchie-pwshvk/docs/infinite-assault.md): on `main` once C1 (#4577) merges, and until then on the planning branch `claude/gallant-ritchie-pwshvk`. Where it and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins (CLAUDE.md). Read its IA11 (the set, its ids, its hold, its tags and the design rules) and the comment CF leaves on
#4601 listing the verbs the set lacks.

Read `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` first (CLAUDE.md rule 10), its rows for a card of a set that has not shipped above
all, and `spec/README.md` with the sections and rulings the cards touch (rule 1).

**Owns:** its cards' script files (`crates/cards/src/scripts/infinite_assault/cNNN_slug.rs`, IA-193 to IA-216
and their tokens), each entry's `loc` (`cargo jackioh catalog loc <path>`), and its own cards' rows in the
shared tables only where its build decides otherwise. CF wrote every other row. A verb, keyword or board fact the
engine lacks goes in the engine by `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §6, in a file of its own where it can, with as few lines
in the shared engine files (`effects/mod.rs`, `script.rs`, `query.rs`, `wire/events.rs`) as possible, and its

## The design rules (IA11)

**The design rules every card part keeps.**

1. **Real cards.** Each card is legal in an ordinary game and plays the same in any mode; none reads the
   mode or its level. Commons to Legendaries of the doctrines and the Core sit on JackiOh's curve (costs
   (0) to (4); about 4 stats at (1), 8 at (2), 12 at (3), 16 at (4) for a Unit with little text, less with
   more), so they can be reused. Commander cards are boss cards, above the curve on purpose.
2. **Spicy, never unfair.** Swingy and rule-bending is the point, but every threat has an answer the player
   can see coming: a countdown is shown, a wall can be killed, a bluff can be called. Nothing makes the
   player lose with no counterplay, and nothing locks them out of playing for a turn they can't foresee
   (Kill Switch, IA-140, fires on a third card, which the player may choose not to play).
3. **Expressible.** The text uses verbs, keywords and filters the engine has (§6); where a card needs a new
   one, its part adds it by `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §6, with its test. Numbers are `params` (`{damage}`),
   never literals (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **Radiant is about twice the base face** (R275): doubled stats and a better line, never stats alone for
   a Unit with text. Each part writes its `docs/radiant-audit.md` rows.
5. **"Infinite Assault card"** in a card's text is a pool that names the set, which reaches the set while
   it is held (R1846001: a pool that names its set keeps to it). "Created" is the engine's Created mark.
6. **The AI must pilot it.** A card whose prompt the AI can't answer well is fixed or redesigned in its
   part, not shipped hoping.
7. **The part may tune.** A part may change a number, a word or a Radiant line where the engine or balance
   asks, keeping the card's role and its spice, and says so in its pull request; a bigger change goes in a
   ruling note.

## Done when

- Every card's script plays its base and Radiant faces by its §8.13 row, with tests in the same file for both
  (CLAUDE.md rule 6), and its `STUB (#4602)` header is gone; its entry's `loc` is the script's.
- Each decision the spec doesn't make has a ruling note in this issue's block, a test named after it, and a
  paragraph in `spec/pending/<this issue>.md` (rule 3).
- Every new prompt is answered by the AI, the random policy and the timeout; `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200
  --cards <each of its ids>` is green; `cargo test -p jackioh-cards` passes for its cards.
- Every number is a named constant or a card `param` (rule 9).
